data.name: Qaifa
data.gender_notes: Qaifa is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'q-f-y', meaning 'to move quickly, to be agile, to be nimble'. The name Qaifa is often used to describe someone who is quick on their feet, both physically and mentally. It can also be used to describe someone who is skillful and dexterous, or someone who is fleet of foot and able to move around obstacles with ease.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes agility and adaptability in the face of challenges, and the ability to move through life with grace and ease.
data.etymology: Qaifa belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Quick, agile, nimble.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Qaifa total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Qaifa holds a rich cultural significance in the Arab world, especially in the context of Arab Bedouin tribes. In the past, the Arab Bedouins relied heavily on their agility and quickness to survive in the desert, making the trait highly valued and admired. Qaifa has become a symbol of strength, courage, and adaptability. The name is often given to children born into Bedouin tribes, as a reminder of the resilience and agility required to thrive in their harsh desert environment.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic spirituality, the name Qaifa holds a deeper significance as a reminder of the importance of quickness in the spiritual journey. Qaifa can be seen as a representation of the need to be quick and agile in responding to the call of Allah, to be nimble and adaptive in following the divine guidance in one's life. It is also a reminder of the importance of being quick to seek forgiveness and make amends when one has strayed from the path of righteousness. In this way, the name Qaifa serves as a constant reminder of the need to be steadfast and resolute in one's spiritual journey, despite the challenges and obstacles that may arise along the way.
